name: Men's rights movement
summary: The men's rights movement holds that law, courts and social institutions disadvantage men and boys, and campaigns on issues such as child custody and child support, false accusations, male-only conscription, domestic violence against men, male suicide and health, and routine infant circumcision. It generally rejects feminism and the claim that society systematically privileges men. It is a loose, largely online and single-issue movement with no economic or wider political programme.
scope: The contemporary English-language men's rights movement as described on Wikipedia and in coverage of its conferences, drawing on its fathers' rights groups, A Voice for Men and Warren Farrell's work. Because it has no doctrine beyond gender issues, most answers outside gender, family and conscription are low-confidence. It excludes the earlier men's liberation movement, and the separatist MGTOW and pickup-artist strands are noted only as variants.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The movement does not take a stance on healthcare systems; it only complains about funding gaps such as prostate cancer research versus women's health, which cuts both ways.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: No documented position; the movement's economic concerns are about alimony, child support and sentencing, not wage floors.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Activists span libertarian and centrist views and the movement has no economic doctrine; no stance is documented.

public-ownership.rationale: Nothing in the movement's issue lists touches ownership of industry; adherents are split along general political lines.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: No stated position; adherents' tax views vary with their general politics, not their men's-rights stance.

unions-good.rationale: The movement does not address unions; its concerns are family courts and state services, so no position can be inferred.

property-fundamental.rationale: Not a topic in the movement's literature, though complaints about alimony and asset division in divorce hint at some property sympathy; adherents are split.

regulate-corporations.rationale: No documented position on corporate regulation; the movement targets government and feminism, not business.

cut-welfare.rationale: Activists criticise welfare and child support as favouring women, but also demand men's services and benefits, so there is no clear line.

worker-ownership.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; no basis for a position.

surveillance-ok.rationale: No documented stance on surveillance; adherents vary.

legalize-drugs.rationale: The movement has no drug policy beyond complaints about harsher male sentencing; adherents are split.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Activists present themselves as victims of censorship and labelling as hate (for example the SPLC listing) and oppose speech codes, but this is inferred rather than a stated plank.

strong-leader.rationale: No stated view on executive power; the movement is oriented to courts and legislation, not leadership.

state-harmful.rationale: The movement criticises state bias but demands state action (shelters, ministries for men, legal reform), so it is not anti-statist; inferred from its policy demands.

limit-guns.rationale: No movement position; adherents differ by national and political background.

empower-police-military.rationale: No stated position; the movement's grievance about police concerns domestic-violence arrest policies rather than overall funding.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not a core issue and adherents are split between sexual-liberty and traditionalist views.

rehabilitation.rationale: The movement complains of harsher sentences for men but has no stated penal philosophy.

traditional-family.rationale: Fathers' rights wings stress fathers' involvement and shared parenting, but the movement also attacks marriage law as unfair to men and MGTOW rejects marriage; adherents are genuinely split. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: No stated position; the movement is not organised around this issue.

abortion-legal.rationale: The movement debates male reproductive choice ('paper abortion') and paternal notification, but has no shared view on legality of abortion itself.

more-religion-public.rationale: No stated position; adherents mix secular online activists and religious fathers' groups.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: The movement has no stance on racial redress; its framing of disadvantage is about sex.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Activists dispute feminist claims that gender roles are imposed, and some cite innate sex differences, though the sources describe this only in passing; adherents vary. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

gradual-change.rationale: The movement seeks policy reform through courts and legislatures but has no stated view on pace of change.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The movement is hostile to UN Women and similar bodies it sees as feminist-led (UN Women lists men's rights among 'anti-rights' movements), so adherents are inferred to resist more power for them.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: No documented position, though some manosphere strands are technology-optimistic; inferred as split.

revolution-justified.rationale: The movement works through advocacy, lawsuits and legislation and distances itself from violence in its public statements; inferred from its methods.

experts-over-public.rationale: Activists distrust academics, social workers and family-court professionals they see as biased against men, and say research is skewed by feminism; inferred.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Nothing in the movement suggests abolishing wages; its grievance about men being valued as providers implies work-and-pay is taken for granted.

one-party-rule.rationale: The movement operates in democratic politics, lobbying legislatures, and has no stated claim for single-party rule; inferred.

democracy-best.rationale: The movement operates within democratic politics but also contains strands that reject electoral participation (MGTOW) or women's suffrage rhetoric; AVFM disavows the latter. No clear position.

natural-rulers.rationale: Mainstream adherents claim equality for men not rule by a natural elite; critics allege male supremacy in some groups, but the typical adherent claims equal treatment.

political-violence-never.rationale: Public statements of main groups stress non-violent advocacy, though the SPLC cites inflammatory material from some; inferred agree for the typical adherent.

war-builds-character.rationale: The movement treats men as expendable in war ('male disposability') and objects to being sent to fight, so it is unlikely to glorify war.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The movement is largely secular and online; no scripture-based programme is documented, though some religious fathers' groups exist.

private-courts-defense.rationale: No documented position; the movement wants family courts reformed rather than privatised.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The movement frames the key conflict as one between the sexes, with men as the disadvantaged side, not as class struggle; inferred.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Activists often reject equality-of-outcome measures such as pay-gap policy and say disparities reflect choices, while demanding equal legal treatment; inferred.

self-interest-moral.rationale: No documented position; the movement frames its aims as justice, though MGTOW emphasises male self-interest.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Activists present their case as one of rights and equal treatment (conscription, custody) and object to duties imposed on men alone, such as the draft and child support.

restore-past-order.rationale: Critics such as Allan call the movement reactionary and others say it opposes a more equal gender order, but adherents claim to seek equality, not restoration; split.

direct-action.rationale: The main groups use lobbying, litigation, conferences and online publishing rather than direct action, though A Voice for Men has run provocative campaigns; inferred.

return-to-foraging.rationale: No sign of primitivism in the movement.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: No connection to Marxism is documented; the movement rejects class-based dictatorship frames; inferred.

taxation-theft.rationale: No documented position, though some libertarian-leaning adherents say so; split.

harm-principle.rationale: No stated view; adherents want legal protection from false accusations and compelled child support but are split on broader state limits.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The movement claims equal individual rights for men and boys and targets group-based preferences for women, but also advocates sex-based categories such as 'men's rights' and fathers' groups; split. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

conscription.rationale: The movement's grievance is the male-only draft and Selective Service registration, which it calls sex discrimination; that is an argument for equal treatment, and its sources take no position on conscription as such.

exit-over-voice.rationale: MGTOW stresses withdrawal from society but this is not about leaving a country; no position.

media-academia-power.rationale: Activists commonly claim that academia and media are dominated by feminist perspectives that marginalise men's issues, which a Hatewatch report on a men's issues conference reflects in its account of speakers. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

hereditarian-race.rationale: No documented position; race is not part of the movement's issue list.

total-state.rationale: The movement criticises state overreach in family and criminal law and does not seek a state directing all of life; inferred.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: No sign of feudal ideas in the movement.

bound-labor.rationale: The movement objects to compulsory burdens on men (draft, child support), so bound labour is inferred as opposed.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Activists appeal to neutral statistics and research on male disadvantage while accusing feminist scholarship of bias, which implies a belief in objective knowledge; inferred.

school-vouchers.rationale: No documented position, though some activists want single-sex classes and alternatives to mainstream schooling for boys; split.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Online strands often present themselves as rationalist, but religious fathers' groups exist; no shared position.

work-for-welfare.rationale: No documented position, though the movement criticises benefits systems for favouring women; split.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Mainstream adherents demand equal legal treatment of men (custody, conscription, domestic-violence services) and attack sex-based legal distinctions, though some strands are traditionalist; the core framing is anti-discrimination.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Race segregation is not part of the movement and its rights-based framing opposes legal classification by group; inferred.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The movement sees the state as biased by sex (towards women), not as an instrument of a ruling class; inferred.

elite-replacement.rationale: No documented position; some manosphere figures touch this theme but it is not part of the movement's agenda.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Activists say patriarchy is a myth and that women hold as much or more power than men; the movement's premise is that men are not privileged relative to women.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: No documented position, though activists distrust politicians they see as pandering to feminist lobbies; split.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: The movement stresses bodily autonomy and paternal reproductive choice and opposes coercion; eugenic policy is inferred to be rejected.

night-watchman-state.rationale: No documented position; the movement seeks state action on family law and male services, but adherents include libertarians.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Not part of the movement; its stated aims do not include discouraging mixed relationships.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Equality before the law between men and women is the movement's stated basis, though critics say some strands treat women as lesser; typical adherent claims equal rights.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: No documented position, though Indian men's groups campaign against laws they see as biased, such as anti-dowry law; no stance on religion-based personal law.

population-transfer.rationale: Not part of the movement; inferred to be opposed given its rights framing.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: No documented position, though some manosphere strands endorse competition; split.

vanguard-party.rationale: The movement is decentralised and has no vanguard organisation.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Activists complain about loss of due-process protections for accused men, and the movement wants those protections strengthened; inferred opposed to suspending them.

party-controls-media.rationale: Activists claim media bias against men and want their views heard, not state control; inferred.

clerical-rule.rationale: No sign of clerical politics in the movement.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: No documented position, though adherents object to male-only conscription.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Activists say they are censored and oppose speech restrictions; inferred.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: No sign of this in the movement.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: No documented position, though activists criticise academia; split.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Activists blame the 'feminization' of schooling for harming boys and criticise gender-equality curricula as one-sided; sex education itself is not a stated issue.

restrict-pornography.rationale: No documented position; adherents are split between libertarian and traditionalist views.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Activists oppose routine infant circumcision, which many religious communities practise, but the movement states no general view on religious exemptions from law.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The movement stresses liberties and due process for men; inferred opposed.

sacred-ruler.rationale: No sign of this in the movement.

character-from-environment.rationale: Activists often cite innate sex differences against feminist environmental accounts, though the sources mention this thinly; inferred.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The movement's rights framing and demands for equal treatment under law imply no one stands above the law; inferred.

decide-locally.rationale: The movement has no stated view on devolution; its demands target national family, criminal and education law.

equal-parenting.rationale: Default equal or joint custody is the central demand of the fathers' rights wing, the main route into the movement.

leader-cult.rationale: No documented position; inferred from the movement's anti-establishment, decentralised online character and distrust of institutions, which sits badly with state-led glorification of leaders.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: The movement has no economic programme and is opposed to left ideologies; inferred as a mild rejection of Marxist doctrine.

land-redistribution.rationale: Inferred from the lack of a programme and from the movement's mostly libertarian and conservative leanings.

refugee-return.rationale: The movement does not address refugee policy.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: The movement does not address territorial claims.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Inferred from the movement's stress on legal equality and individual rights; it takes no position on religion.

women-must-cover.rationale: Inferred from its opposition to laws that treat the sexes differently, and its lack of religious doctrine.

common-currency.rationale: The movement is indifferent to monetary union.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: The movement is indifferent to supranational unity.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: The movement is indifferent to minority autonomy.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Inferred from its own strategy of seeking legal equality for men within existing states through courts and legislatures.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Inferred from its stress on biological sex differences and choices over social structure; no source states a view on historical materialism.

ban-cartels.rationale: The movement has no economic programme and does not address cartels.

no-bailouts.rationale: The movement has no economic programme and does not address bailouts.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Adherents complain that courts disadvantage men but seek reform rather than majority rule over courts; inferred as split.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: The movement opposes feminist quota policies as unequal treatment, though sources document this mainly in general terms.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: The movement has no trade programme.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: The movement has no trade programme.

moral-incentives.rationale: Inferred from its general individualism and the absence of any collectivist programme.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Inferred from its legalist, reformist strategy and focus on courts and public debate.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The movement does not address hereditary privilege.

history-own-civilization.rationale: No documented position; the movement is about gender issues, not curriculum.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Inferred from the movement's general rejection of paternalism and claimed hierarchies of privilege; not documented.

patriotic-education.rationale: No documented position; activists range across the political spectrum on patriotism.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Inferred from the demand for equal treatment of men and rejection of group-based preferences; not explicitly stated for race.

public-money-creation.rationale: No documented position; the movement has no economic doctrine.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: No documented position; economic doctrine is absent.

former-empire-influence.rationale: No documented position on foreign policy.

delink-world-market.rationale: No documented position on trade or development.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Not addressed; the movement is focused on gender, not class.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Activists want anti-discrimination law applied to men while many libertarian-leaning members oppose it; adherents are split.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: No documented position, though activists invoke equal rights under law and are split on constitutional design.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: No documented position; the movement is single-issue on gender and family law.

elective-rulers.rationale: No documented position on succession or monarchy.

minority-veto.rationale: Inferred: the movement stresses individual rights and due process, but has no stated view on consent rules for groups.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: No documented position; the movement criticizes courts and institutions without a theory of resistance.

parliament-supreme.rationale: No documented position on lawmaking authority.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Not addressed; strands vary, some echo anti-feminist suspicion of animal rights while others are indifferent.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Inferred: no stance on animals, and mainstream attitudes in its largely Western base accept humane use.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Inferred: the movement rejects the view that men owe special duties as a privileged class and denies male privilege.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The movement is organized around political and legal campaigns, so withdrawal is contrary to it, though the MGTOW strand withdraws from relationships.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Many in the movement hold that media and culture promote misandry and a feminist social order; this is an inference from its critique of media.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: No documented position; the movement does not use hegemony theory, though it claims feminist culture shapes institutions.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: No documented position on world-economy theory.

native-born-offices.rationale: No documented position on reserving offices for natives.

party-own-road.rationale: Not applicable; the movement is not a communist or socialist current.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: No documented position on development aid.

return-lost-territory.rationale: No documented position on territorial claims.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: No documented position on indigenous political leadership.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Inferred: the movement opposes feminism and the left generally, and is not framed around anti-fascism as a constitutional value.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: No documented position on the Civil War.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: The movement's core claim is that boys and men face neglected disadvantage in education, health and suicide, and Farrell's work centers on this.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Domestic violence against men is a named issue area for the movement, which demands equal recognition and services.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: No documented position on civilizational variety of institutions.

military-guardian-role.rationale: No documented position on the military's political role.

paid-care-work.rationale: The movement generally disputes feminist claims that household labor is exploited; this is a mild lean against wages for housework, inferred from its critique of feminism.

filial-duty.rationale: The movement has no documented position on adult children's duties to parents; its family focus is fathers' custody and support.

office-by-exam.rationale: No documented position; the movement's concerns are gender-based laws, not how public posts are filled.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: No documented position; the movement has no economic programme beyond alimony, support and sentencing.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Activists complain about divorce courts, alimony and custody outcomes but split on easy divorce itself, so no stated position.

recallable-delegates.rationale: No documented position on delegate democracy; the movement is a single-issue, mostly online current.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: No documented position; activists range from libertarian to centrist and pension design is not a movement issue.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Inferred from the movement's libertarian-leaning wing and focus on individual property in divorce settlements; no stated position on land tenure.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Inferred from the movement's reliance on ordinary liberal-democratic institutions to win legal reform; no source addresses budgets.

single-official-language.rationale: No documented position on language policy; the movement is concerned with gender issues only.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: No documented position on foreign land ownership; not part of the movement's issue list.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Inferred: the movement rejects the claim that society systematically privileges one group and argues about intent in custody and sentencing, so outcome-based discrimination framing is disfavoured.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: No documented position; the movement's critiques target feminism and family law, not consumer culture.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: No documented position on foreign policy; not part of the movement's issue list.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: No documented position on foreign policy; not part of the movement's issue list.

corporate-influence.rationale: The movement has no economic programme and takes no side on lobbying.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: No documented position; adherents are not defined by a view on foreign funding.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Fathers' rights groups focus on custody and support rather than birth-rate policy, and the issue is not addressed.

residents-only-property.rationale: The movement has no stance on property purchase rules.

job-guarantee.rationale: No economic doctrine; adherents range from libertarian to left, so the movement is indifferent.

democratic-peace.rationale: The movement does not address foreign policy or the democratic peace.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Adherents complain that courts and laws are biased against men, but no general stance on a duty to obey is documented.

non-intervention.rationale: The movement takes no position on foreign policy.

industrial-unions.rationale: No documented position on union organisation.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Not part of the movement's platform; its grievances target feminism and family law, not a minority's plot, though fringe voices differ.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Adherents are split: fathers' rights groups want fairer marriage and divorce law, while some voices urge men to avoid marriage.

public-access-to-information.rationale: The movement does not address government information, though it does press for records on family courts.

local-production.rationale: No documented position on local production.

informal-organisation.rationale: The movement is loose and largely online, but fathers' rights groups also form lasting organisations, so adherents are split.

national-law-over-international.rationale: No documented position on international law.

religious-nation.rationale: No documented position; the movement is organised around gender and family issues, not nationhood or religion.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: The movement has no foreign-policy programme; the sources do not address it.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: The movement has no fiscal programme; the sources do not address it.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The movement is single-issue on gender; the sources discuss no economic ownership position.

defeat-communism.rationale: No anti-communism or foreign-policy stance is documented; the movement is a loose gender-issue movement.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: The movement has no economic or public-service programme; the sources do not address it.

religion-illusion.rationale: The movement has no position on religion; the sources are silent.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: The movement has no economic doctrine, so no view on capitalism's historical role is documented.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The movement rejects feminism and the claim that women are systematically subordinated, so a feminist case for economic transformation is rejected. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

socialized-care.rationale: Inferred: the movement prizes parental rights for fathers and equal custody and would likely resist replacing family care with state services; not stated.

purge-loanwords.rationale: The movement has no language policy; the sources do not address it.

treaties-binding.rationale: The movement has no position on treaties with internal nations; the sources do not address it.

cooperative-communities.rationale: The movement has no programme for communal society; the sources do not address it.

majority-settlement.rationale: The movement has no position on settlement policy; the sources do not address it.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The movement has no economic programme and its adherents hold no common view on capitalism versus communism.

historical-land-claim.rationale: The movement has no position on land claims; this is outside its gender-focused agenda.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Inferred: not part of the agenda, and nothing in the sources links the movement to denial.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Inferred: the movement is a single-issue gender campaign with no stated line on criminalisation, and its libertarian streak leans against it.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Inferred: the movement campaigns as a rights group seeking legal reform, which sits badly with suppressing opposition.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Inferred: it has no religious programme and its civil-rights framing leans against state enforcement of religion.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Inferred: outside its agenda, with no sign of imperial sympathies in the sources.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Inferred: this religious doctrine is outside the movement's concerns and nothing in the sources supports it.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Inferred: the movement works through courts and legislatures, not religious claims about rulers.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The movement has no stated view on workplace or community democracy; it is a loose, largely online single-issue campaign.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: The movement rejects feminism and the claim that society systematically privileges men, which this framework presupposes. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Inferred: adherents are mixed, but the movement's focus on men's disadvantage and its hostility to feminism lean against it.

assisted-dying.rationale: Male suicide is a campaign issue but the sources give no stance on assisted dying, so adherents are treated as split.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Inferred: the movement has no wider programme and draws members from across the spectrum.

alienated-labor.rationale: Inferred: the movement has no economic programme and its critique of feminism rather than capitalism points away from this claim.

islam-incompatible.rationale: The movement has no position on this; members are mixed and it is not on the agenda.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Inferred: the movement is secular and rights-based, with no theological doctrine of authority.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: The movement has no stated position on religious dress; it is outside its agenda.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Inferred: the movement stresses false accusations and due process for the accused, which cuts against limiting the tools used to settle harassment claims.

social-market-economy.rationale: The movement has no economic programme, so no position can be stated.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Inferred: it opposes male-only conscription but wants equal treatment or an end to the draft, not abolition of armed forces.

rich-first.rationale: The movement has no economic programme; adherents are split.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: The movement has no foreign-policy position.

dynastic-succession.rationale: The movement has no position on political succession; it is a single-issue gender movement with no wider programme.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: The movement takes no position on banking; it has no economic programme beyond gender issues.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: The movement does not address international lenders; it campaigns on gender and family law only.

property-franchise.rationale: Inferred from its campaign for equal treatment of men in law; a property franchise is not discussed, and a universal-rights framing is more likely.

domination-women-nature.rationale: The movement rejects feminism and the claim that society systematically dominates women, so adherents would reject linking and ending the two forms of domination together. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

reification.rationale: The movement has no economic doctrine; a Marxist theory of reification is foreign to a movement that mostly rejects structural critiques of society.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: The movement does not address press ownership; it complains that media coverage of men's issues is hostile, which does not settle this claim.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Adherents campaign for due process in courts, which implies rule by known law, but the movement has no doctrine on rulers and decrees; inferred.

racial-franchise.rationale: The movement claims equal rights for men and women and has no racial platform; coverage of its conferences records no such restriction. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

online-participation.rationale: The movement is largely online, but it has no stated position on internet voting or deliberation.

open-government-data.rationale: The movement has no stance on government transparency, though it distrusts family courts for opacity; inferred, so neutral.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: The movement has no religious programme, and a legal limit on interfaith marriage is not part of its gender agenda; inferred.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: The movement is organised around gender and has no religious-minority agenda; boycotts of minority-owned shops are not part of it, and adherents would disavow them.

citizens-assembly.rationale: The movement has no position on democratic procedure; the sources discuss only gender-related issues.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: The movement has no doctrine on religion; sources do not address it and adherents vary in belief.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The movement has no economic programme and its adherents range from libertarian to conservative to left, so it is split on this; inferred from its single-issue focus on gender.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: The movement does not address gay service; its military focus is the male-only draft, and adherents differ on LGBT issues, so this is inferred as split.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Inferred: the movement stresses individual rights and has a sizeable religious and conservative wing, and nothing in its issue list supports state promotion of belief.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Inferred: the movement complains of unequal sentencing and false accusations but wants fairer courts and policing, not their abolition.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: The movement has no position on constitutional design for ethnic or sectarian divisions; adherents are split and it is outside its gender focus.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Adherents are split between market-minded and welfare-supporting views, and the movement's own complaints concern unequal services for men, not who should deliver aid.

term-limits.rationale: No stated position; the movement is a single-issue one and adherents are split on political structure, so this is inferred as neutral.

vote-delegation.rationale: The movement has no position on delegated voting; this is outside its programme and adherents are split.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: The movement does not discuss extinction risk; its concern with male suicide and health is a different priority, so adherents are split or indifferent.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Adherents are split, with secular equal-treatment advocates alongside religious traditionalists; the movement takes no line on religious offices.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred: the movement argues for equal legal treatment of the sexes and equal parenting rather than male headship, though some traditionalist adherents dissent.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: The movement has no position on immigration or resident voting; adherents are split.

rent-control.rationale: The movement has no economic programme; adherents are split.

abolish-ip.rationale: No stated position; the movement is focused on gender and family issues.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred from its emphasis on individual male rights and criticism of state-led mobilisation; not discussed.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: No stated position outside gender and family issues.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: No stated position outside gender and family issues.

recognise-genocide.rationale: No stated position; genocide recognition is outside its issues.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The movement has no economic programme; adherents are split.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Inferred from its sympathy for men who defend themselves and its complaints about legal treatment of men who use force in defence.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: No stated position; the movement is not nationalist as such.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: It rejects feminist claims that gender roles are wholly constructed, favouring innate differences, but the sex question is not addressed directly.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: It rejects feminist theory and generally treats women as a coherent group; inferred.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: No stated position; outside its issues.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Inferred from its secular, grievance-based focus; no spiritual framing is documented.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: No stated position outside gender issues.

culture-before-state.rationale: No stated position outside gender issues.

god-not-male.rationale: No stated position; the movement is mostly secular and does not address theology.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: It opposes judging institutions by feminist criteria, so a women-centred test of scripture would be rejected; inferred.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: No stated position outside gender issues.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: No stated position outside gender issues.

independent-unions.rationale: The movement has no economic programme and does not address unions.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The movement has no position on what counts as socialism.

local-essentials-public.rationale: The movement has no economic programme, so local ownership of services is not addressed.

second-chamber.rationale: The movement does not address legislative structure.

municipal-property.rationale: Inferred from a largely libertarian-leaning, online adherent base; the movement itself takes no stance.

confederal-coordination.rationale: The movement does not address local government structure.

family-wage.rationale: Adherents criticize the male provider burden but the movement takes no line on a family wage.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: The movement does not address drug regulation.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Inferred from its complaints about male health and shorter male lifespan and gaps in health research funding.

anonymous-payments.rationale: The movement does not address payments.

online-anonymity.rationale: Inferred from the movement's largely online, pseudonymous organizing and fear of doxxing and harassment.

person-over-state.rationale: Inferred from the movement's complaint that courts and institutions sacrifice individual men's interests to feminist or state policy goals.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The movement does not address spiritual questions.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: The movement does not address regional government.

gm-crops.rationale: The movement does not address agriculture.

dense-cities.rationale: The movement does not address urban form.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The movement organizes by sex, and adherents commonly criticize identity politics, so organizing by race is rejected; inferred, not stated.

racial-pride.rationale: The movement takes no stance on racial pride.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: The movement objects to male-only conscription but takes no stance on when wars are justified.

language-defines-nation.rationale: The movement has no stated position on nationhood; it is single-issue on gender.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred from its demand for equal treatment under law regardless of group.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Not addressed; the movement is a gender-issue movement with no foreign-policy programme.

free-public-college.rationale: Not addressed; some members point to men falling behind in college, but there is no common position on tuition.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Inferred from a largely libertarian-leaning online base that distrusts new taxes; not stated.

future-generations.rationale: Inferred: no stated position, but a general pro-family and pro-children stance makes agreement likely.

women-distinct-values.rationale: The movement rejects feminism and the claim that women's values deserve special weight; it argues men are the group left unheard.

arms-reduction.rationale: Not addressed, apart from its opposition to male-only conscription.

capital-controls.rationale: Inferred from its libertarian-leaning base; not stated.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: The movement has no stated line on gun control or armed groups; its gender-issue focus leaves adherents split.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: It objects to male-only conscription but campaigns for equal treatment, not for soldiers to disobey orders; inferred from that issue list.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Labour relations are outside its gender-issues agenda and adherents are split; inferred as indifferent.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: It has no economic programme; inferred as indifferent, since tax credits for working families cut both ways for its fathers' rights concerns.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: It has no economic programme, and adherents range from libertarian to centrist.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: International economic rules are outside a single-issue gender movement; no position found.

smash-state-machine.rationale: It campaigns to reform courts and laws on custody, paternity and domestic violence rather than to overthrow the state; inferred from that reformist issue list.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: It has no economic blueprint and adherents are split; inferred as indifferent.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Ecosystem accounting is outside its agenda; no position found.

sacred-nation.rationale: It is an individualist, largely online movement that frames itself around men's grievances, not national community; inferred.

student-debt-relief.rationale: It has no stance on student loans, though its boy-crisis education concerns could cut either way.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Regional exploitation is outside its agenda, and its individualist framing makes it unlikely to adopt this claim; inferred.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Farrell and others stress innate sex differences and shared male and female needs rather than purely social construction; inferred from that emphasis.

public-service-media.rationale: Adherents regard mainstream media as hostile to men and misandrist, so they are unlikely to back state-funded media; inferred.

religions-one-truth.rationale: The movement has no religious doctrine and its members span believers and atheists; this is inferred from it being a single-issue gender movement.

farm-price-support.rationale: Farm policy is outside the movement's concerns and its largely online supporters are split on economics, so this is a neutral inference.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: The movement takes no line on defence; nothing in its sources addresses nuclear arms, so adherents are treated as split.

workers-own-party.rationale: The movement is mostly liberal-individualist or conservative in economics and campaigns on gender, not class; a class party is not part of its aims, inferred from its lack of an economic programme.

ban-fgm.rationale: Adherents commonly argue that male circumcision should be treated alike, which usually means banning both rather than neither, but some use the point to attack feminism; inferred from the intactivist strand in s1.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Movement texts demand formal legal equality and do not defend male-only inheritance, but the issue is not discussed; inferred from its equal-treatment rhetoric.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Language naming is unrelated to the movement's issues; no stance is documented.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: The movement has no environmental programme and its libertarian and conservative wings would split on this; no stance is documented.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: The movement is an English-language, mostly Western, liberal-democratic one with no interest in traditional leaders; inferred as mild disagreement from its appeal to equal treatment under state law.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Its emphasis on individual rights against institutions suggests liberty should not give way, but it has no environmental stance; inferred at low confidence.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Adherents complain of harsh sentencing of men and false accusations, which points against rigid rules, yet many are tough-on-crime conservatives; split.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Immigration is outside the movement's scope and its supporters are politically mixed; no stance is documented.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Inferred: the movement's libertarian-leaning online wing backs individual choice and many members oppose compulsory dues, though it has no labour programme.

voter-id.rationale: Inferred: no source states a position, but the movement leans right on fairness and fraud claims and is hostile to what it sees as unequal rules.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: The movement has no religious doctrine, and the sources do not address the question.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: The movement has no view on democracy as procedure; its sources cover only gender issues.

premarital-sex.rationale: A Voice for Men and Farrell argue against the double standard that stigmatises sexual freedom for women while ignoring men's, and treat sexual choice as the same for both sexes. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: The movement has no position on internet policy; its sources cover only gender, family and law.

negative-income-tax.rationale: The movement has no economic programme, so adherents are split and the sources never discuss welfare reform.

women-suffrage.rationale: The movement frames its demand as equal legal treatment for men and women and opposes feminism, not women's vote; inferred, as suffrage itself is not discussed.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: A Voice for Men and Farrell reject the feminist view that women are systemically oppressed, and treat religion as not a major cause. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

race-social-construct.rationale: The movement has no stated view on racial categories; its sources cover only gender issues.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: The movement rejects feminism and campaigns against women-only state programmes and agencies, arguing they ignore male disadvantage and so are one-sided.

homestead-ownership.rationale: The movement has no economic programme; property acquisition is not discussed.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: The movement does not address international criminal law.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Outside gender issues the movement takes no stance on religion.

gendered-self-government.rationale: The movement campaigns for men's issues, not on Indigenous self-government; it is not discussed.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Inferred from the movement's general suspicion of state-driven agendas and its lack of any planned-economy tradition.

indirect-election.rationale: The movement has no position on electoral structure.

national-church-status.rationale: The movement takes no stance on national churches.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: The movement does not address ethnic autonomy.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: The movement does not address territorial disputes.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: The movement does not address colonial borders.

simple-living.rationale: The movement has no position on lifestyle or self-sufficiency.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: The movement does not address indigenous settlement.

equal-conscription.rationale: Male-only conscription is one of the movement's named campaign issues, and its demand is equal treatment of men and women under any draft.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: The movement has no doctrine beyond gender issues; a spiritual bond with the homeland is not discussed in the sources.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: The movement has no stated position on drug policy or killing without trial, and its due-process complaints point towards opposing it.

close-ties-china.rationale: The movement has no foreign or economic programme beyond gender issues.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: The movement has no stated position on kin minorities abroad.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Resource ownership is outside the movement's gender-focused agenda.

self-ownership.rationale: Inferred from its stress on bodily autonomy and individual rights against family courts, though the term is not used in the sources.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Taxation is outside the movement's gender-focused agenda.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Social spending is outside the agenda, apart from complaints about funding for male-specific health services.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: The movement has no stated view on parties and leaders.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Business privileges are outside the movement's agenda.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Religious denominations are outside the movement's agenda.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: The movement has no stated view on technology and ancestral values.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: The movement campaigns for men's equal treatment in family law; divorce initiation is not a stated issue and members are split.

national-resource-control.rationale: Resource control is outside the movement's gender-focused agenda.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Inferred from the movement's focus on process and fairness for men; it has no economic doctrine.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: The movement has no economic programme and takes no position on this tax.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Inferred from its rejection of the idea that society systematically privileges one group; race is not a topic it addresses.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Inferred from its complaints about family courts and custody and support rulings it holds to be unjust.

automate-paid-work.rationale: The movement does not discuss automation and work, beyond complaints about male-dominated dangerous jobs.

multipolar-world.rationale: The movement is single-issue and has no stated foreign-policy position.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: The movement has no economic doctrine and takes no position on value theory.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Inferred from its largely nationalist, anti-feminist online audience; no source states it.

material-over-identity.rationale: Inferred from its rejection of identity-based campaigns by other groups, though it runs its own gender-based campaign.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Inferred from its generally anti-left stance; no source discusses market socialism.

missingStatements.text: Courts should presume that children of separated parents spend equal time with each parent.
missingStatements.rationale: Joint custody as the default is the central demand of the fathers' rights wing, the main route into the movement.

missingStatements.text: Men and women should be treated identically in law on military conscription.
missingStatements.rationale: The male-only draft is framed as sex discrimination by the movement; adherents want it ended or extended to women.
missingStatements.declined: The existing conscription statement covers the draft question and a male-only-draft statement is too narrow to keep the bank lean.

missingStatements.text: Routine circumcision of infant boys for non-medical reasons should be banned.
missingStatements.rationale: Most members oppose it and compare it to female genital mutilation, and bodily autonomy is a listed issue area.
missingStatements.declined: Infant circumcision is a narrow single-issue topic with low inclusion across ideologies.

missingStatements.text: A man should be able to avoid legal parenthood for a child he did not choose to father, including by testing paternity or opting out before birth.
missingStatements.rationale: Paternity testing, relief from support for non-biological children and 'paper abortion' are advocated, with paternity listed among core issues.
missingStatements.declined: Paternity opt-out and "paper abortion" is a niche demand within the movement; too narrow for the bank.

missingStatements.text: Women's violence against men in intimate relationships is as significant as men's violence against women and deserves equal shelter and services.
missingStatements.rationale: Activists claim near-symmetry in domestic violence and campaign for shelters for abused men.

notes: Fringe strands (MGTOW, red pill) and the groups the SPLC listed as male supremacist would answer gender questions more extremely; critics argue the movement is defined by backlash against feminism. Almost every non-gender answer is an inference, so the profile may fail the inclusion check.
